name: Shakespeare's Century: Tudors, Stuarts and the Globe
description: The playwright and the age that made him: Tudor and Stuart monarchs, the Armada, the Globe on the Thames, the great tragedies, and the afterlife of his plays on stage and screen.

checkpoints.name: The Tudor crown
checkpoints.note: Richard III dies at Bosworth in 1485 and the House of Tudor takes the throne. Henry VIII breaks with Rome and founds the Church of England, and in 1558 his daughter Elizabeth I is crowned. These are the kings and quarrels that Shakespeare will later put on the stage.

checkpoints.name: Elizabeth's England
checkpoints.note: William Shakespeare is born in Stratford in 1564 and is writing for the London stage by the early 1590s. Francis Drake sails round the world, Mary, Queen of Scots, is executed, and the Spanish Armada is beaten in 1588. A Midsummer Night's Dream and Romeo and Juliet win the crowds.

checkpoints.name: The Globe years
checkpoints.note: Shakespeare's company opens the Globe Theatre on the south bank of the Thames in 1599, and Hamlet soon follows. When Elizabeth dies in 1603, James I brings in the House of Stuart and takes the players under his name. Othello, King Lear and Macbeth appear as the Gunpowder Plot fails and Don Quixote is published in Spain.

checkpoints.name: Last plays and the Folio
checkpoints.note: The Tempest is among Shakespeare's last plays, and he dies in 1616, the same year as Miguel de Cervantes. Francis Bacon, lawyer and philosopher, rises to Lord Chancellor in 1618. In 1623 friends publish the First Folio, saving half his plays from being lost, and in 1642 the Globe closes when the theatres are shut.

checkpoints.name: The afterlife
checkpoints.note: Shakespeare's words and phrases sink deep into the English language, and his plays travel the world. Giuseppe Verdi turns Macbeth and Othello into operas, and Akira Kurosawa retells Macbeth and King Lear on film as stories of feudal Japan.
